_note: Original items written for json-inference's `bench --quality` (2026-10-17). Small on purpose; answers are exact.

math.prompt: A bakery sells muffins in boxes of 6. It bakes 18 trays of 80 muffins each. How many muffins does it bake in total? End your reply with the number.
Mia has 52 stickers. She gives 9 to her brother and twice as many to her friend. Then she buys 12 more. How many stickers does she have now? End your reply with the number.
A train travels at 90 km/h for 2 hours and then at 45 km/h for 1 hour. How many kilometres does it travel in total? End your reply with the number.
A rectangle has a perimeter of 48 cm and its length is 10 cm more than its width. What is its length in cm? End your reply with the number.
Tickets cost $13 for adults and $8 for children. A school group buys 16 adult and 13 child tickets. How many dollars do they pay? End your reply with the number.
The average of five numbers is 21. Four of them are 12, 18, 20 and 26. What is the fifth number? End your reply with the number.
What is 45 squared? End your reply with the number.
A full tank holds 350 litres. A pump removes 75 litres per minute while a hose adds 25 litres per minute. After how many minutes is the tank empty? End your reply with the number.

instructions.prompt: List three benefits of regular exercise. Reply with exactly three lines, each starting with '- ', and nothing else.
Describe the ocean in one sentence. Use only lowercase letters; no capital letters anywhere.
Give the capital of Japan as a JSON object with exactly the keys "city" and "country". Reply with the JSON only.
Describe a sunset in exactly five words. Reply with those five words only.
Name two primary colors, then end your reply with the word DONE in capital letters.
Write a short sentence about a cat without using the letter 'e' anywhere. Reply with the sentence only.
